data.title: Vallourec's core profit falls 26%, hit by Iran war and disruption in the US
data.description:
Key points:
  • Q3 EBITDA falls 26% to $181 million, in line with Vallourec's guidance
  • Q4 core earnings seen in the same $170-210 million range
  • Shares fall 12% in early Paris trading as lack of Q4 recovery disappoints

By Mathias de Rozario and Rihab Latrache

Steel tubes maker Vallourec reported a 25.8% drop in its third-quarter core profit on Friday, impacted by the Iran war and a temporary operational disruption in the US, and said it did not expect an improvement in the fourth quarter.

The French company's shares fell more than 12% in early trading, the worst performer on the SBF 120 index of Paris' most traded stocks.

Vallourec, which provides tubing for oil and gas, low-carbon energy and industrial markets, has been impacted by rising costs, particularly in logistics, due to the conflict in the Middle East, and delivery delays caused by severe congestion in the ports south of the Strait of Hormuz.

Its earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization fell to $181 million but were within the previously communicated range of $170 million to $210 million. Fourth-quarter EBITDA is seen in the same range, Vallourec said.

Analysts from TP ICAP Midcap said the outlook for the last three months of the year was disappointing, as it effectively postpones the expected earnings recovery until 2027.

"The temporary operational issue in our US business is also expected to constrain the sequential improvement we had anticipated in the fourth quarter," CEO Philippe Guillemot said in a statement.

A third-party operator at one of Vallourec’s US plants slowed a production line during the third quarter, so the company could not produce and deliver as much as it had planned from the end of the third quarter to the beginning of the fourth, Guillemot added in a call with journalists.

Sales volumes in Vallourec's Tubes business fell 10% from last year to 274,000 metric tons.

Guillemot said Middle East tube inventories had fallen sharply, making restocking essential for drilling operations, a significant demand source for Vallourec.

The company expects the war-linked extra costs to be largely reimbursed by customers over the coming quarters.

data.title: Midwest Energy wins 1,200-tonne rare earth magnet project under Centre's ₹7,280-cr scheme
data.description:
Midwest Energy Ltd has been selected to set up a 1,200-tonne-per-annum (MTPA) rare earth permanent magnet manufacturing project under the Centre’s ₹7,280-crore incentive scheme, marking a step forward in India’s efforts to build domestic capacity for materials critical to electric mobility, renewable energy and advanced manufacturing.

The company, in a statement, said it has received a Letter of Intent (LOI) from the Ministry of Heavy Industries after emerging as a successful bidder under the Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnets (REPM). It quoted a sales incentive rate of ₹505.05 per kg for the project.

The LOI is conditional, with Midwest Energy required to furnish a performance security of ₹40 crore within 90 days of its receipt.

The government will issue the final Letter of Award after verifying that the company has met the stipulated conditions under the scheme and the request for proposal, the company said in a statement on Friday.

Midwest Energy has already invested ₹250 crore in a rare earth permanent magnet manufacturing facility in Hyderabad. Its Phase-I plant, with an initial capacity of 500 tonnes per annum, is currently undergoing commissioning.

The company aims to scale up its manufacturing capacity to 1,500 MTPA by the end of 2027, it said.

The government-backed scheme is intended to establish an integrated domestic manufacturing ecosystem for sintered rare earth permanent magnets, reducing India’s reliance on imported supplies of these strategically important materials.

“The Letter of Intent marks an important milestone in Midwest Energy’s journey towards building domestic capabilities in rare earth permanent magnet manufacturing. With our Hyderabad facility progressing through commissioning, we are focused on developing indigenous manufacturing capabilities and contributing to India’s efforts to build a more resilient and self-reliant supply chain for critical materials. We see significant long-term opportunities across electric mobility, renewable energy and other advanced industrial applications,” said Soumya Kollareddy, Whole-Time Director and Chief Executive Officer.

Sintered neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) magnets are among the strongest commercially available permanent magnets and are used in electric vehicle motors, wind turbine generators, industrial equipment, consumer electronics and several aerospace and defence applications.

Their importance has grown alongside the expansion of electric mobility and renewable energy, where high-performance magnets enable compact, efficient motors and generators.

India’s dependence on imported rare earth magnets exposes manufacturers to supply-chain disruptions, price volatility and geopolitical risks. Developing domestic manufacturing capabilities is therefore a strategic priority, particularly as the country seeks to expand its electric vehicle and clean energy industries.

The Centre’s ₹7,280-crore REPM scheme is aimed at addressing this vulnerability by incentivising domestic production of sintered permanent magnets and encouraging investment in the manufacturing value chain.

Midwest Energy’s rare earth magnet investment forms part of a broader push into emerging energy technologies.

The company has also established a battery energy storage systems (BESS) manufacturing facility in Bengaluru with an annual capacity of 1.2 GWh, backed by an investment of about ₹100 crore.

data.title: Global Bond Yields Fall as Investors Seek Safe-Haven Assets — Update
data.description:
By Miriam Mukuru

Yields on U.S., U.K., and eurozone government bonds dropped on Friday as risk-off sentiment continued to drive demand to safe-haven assets.

The 10-year Treasury yield fell 5.6 basis points to 4.996%, while the U.K. 10-year yield dropped 4.5 bps to 5.271%, according to Tradeweb. Ten-year German Bund yields declined 6.2 bps to 3.339%.

A record initial public offering by Anthropic, which raised $81 billion, failed to revive appetite for artificial-intelligence stocks. Investors continued to question whether the enormous investments in the AI industry would pay off given the rising public resistance toward the industry.

"The blockbuster debut [IPO] couldn't sweep those worries under the rug," Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote, said in a note.

Asian and European stocks sold off on Friday as sentiment continued to deteriorate even after some positive news in the tech industry this week.

"When neither a blockbuster Nvidia beat nor the largest IPO in history can lift the tape, market psychology has fundamentally flipped from dip-buying to structural de-risking," Patrick Munnelly, partner at Tickmill Group, said in a note.

High borrowing costs also raise concerns about AI companies' ability to continue raising funds to finance their massive expansion.

"The scale of the Democratic win in the midterm [elections] has deepened worry that policymakers could push for slower data-center spending," David Groman, global equity strategist at Citi, said in a note.

The concerns about the tech and AI sector are driving the flight to safety, causing government bond yields to drop, Groman said.

data.title: Taiwan stock exchange says it will ensure stable operation of capital markets
data.description:
The Taiwan Stock Exchange will ensure the stable operation of capital markets and investors should remain confident in the fundamentals of Taiwanese companies, its chairman said on Friday, as shares on the bourse suffered another sharp decline.

Taiwan is a leading ​producer of the advanced chips driving AI's rapid expansion, but investors in its tech-heavy bourse have seen their confidence in the boom's future shaken, notably by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation last week.

Taiwan stocks TWSE:TAIEX tumbled more than 6% on Friday and recorded their worst week in more than three decades as investors continued to unwind AI-related bets over concerns around valuations, profitability and rising debt.

Bourse chairman Sherman Lin said in a statement that Taiwan's capital markets are closely linked to international markets and cannot avoid being affected in the short term by international political and economic conditions and market sentiment.

However, Taiwan has sound economic fundamentals and global demand for AI computing still has room for medium- to long-term growth, he said.

"Taiwan's competitive advantage is a complete industrial ecosystem accumulated over many years, with deep strength from semiconductor manufacturing and advanced packaging to AI servers and system integration," Lin said.

"That leading international AI companies keep expanding cooperation with Taiwanese firms also underscores Taiwan's key position in the global technology supply chain."

Lin added that the financial regulator had already imposed new short-selling restrictions and that the exchange will also continue to monitor market conditions and, together with the competent authority, review and adjust the measures as appropriate.

Earlier on Friday, Taiwan's economy ministry said export orders rose more than expected in October to $123.82 billion and at the fastest clip on record, buoyed by worldwide demand for the island's AI chips and technology.

data.title: U.K. Retail Sales Resilience Unlikely to Last — Market Talk
data.description: Retail sales held up well in October, but this momentum is expected to slow going forward, Paul Dales at Capital Economics says in a note. Sales rose 0.7% on the month, supported by a pickup in clothing and food sales. However, this reflected a bump from seasonal weather given retailers' new autumn and winter ranges, Dales says. "And the 0.8% rise in food sales might not be so strong in the coming months since some of it was due to household 'prepping' by buying UHT [milk] and tinned goods." "We doubt that the continued resilience of real retail spending in October can last." (don.forbes@wsj.com)

data.title: Nasdaq Set for Fresh Decline as AI Selloff Intensifies
data.description:
By Joe Stonor

Global stocks sold off and Treasurys strengthened as investor confidence in the artificial-intelligence trade showed signs of cracking.

Nasdaq futures dropped 1.15%, extending sharp falls from the last session. S&P 500 futures fell 0.5%, while contracts tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.1%. Major U.S. indexes are on track for their worst week since the announcement of President Trump's Liberation Day tariffs upended global trade in April 2025.

Anthropic's record-breaking IPO failed to stem heavy selling across global stocks. Chip makers, tech giants and cloud-computing stocks weakened in U.S. premarket trade after heavy selling across Asian tech names. The memory chip-dominated Kospi closed 5.2% lower, while Japan's Nikkei also fell more than 5%. Taiwan's Taiex sank 6.2%, bringing its weekly loss to more than 17%--its worst week since 1990.

The selling bled to European stocks, too. ASML, the continent's most valuable stock, fell more than 5% as a basket of the continent's tech stocks opened 3% lower. The continent-wide Stoxx 600 was 1.2% lower.

Demand for Anthropic's IPO is focusing attention on the sustainability of the AI investment buildout while also draining liquidity from the broader market, said Roger Lee, head of equity strategy at Cavendish.

The gloominess in stock market sentiment comes despite fresh declines for oil. Benchmark Brent crude contracts dropped around 1.25% to $90.85 a barrel. West Texas Intermediate contracts fell 1.7% to trade around $81.80 a barrel. The U.S. Energy Information Administration said Thursday that oil shipments through major Middle Eastern shipping routes increased 19% in the third quarter.

Lower oil prices and an investor flight to safety combined to strengthen Treasurys. Ten-year yields fell back below 5.000%, while two-year yields dropped 6 basis points to 4.720%. Thirty-year yields fell 3.1 basis points to trade around 5.370%.

Metals prices continued to sell off, with gold tumbling close to 3% at $3,580 a troy ounce. The dollar held near multimonth highs, while bitcoin rebounded slightly but remained near July lows, hovering just below $62,000.

For the day ahead, macro watchers will look to Michigan's consumer sentiment index for November, and to Federal Reserve speakers including Christopher Waller.

data.title: Diesel markets recover slightly; east-west remains supportive for jet fuel
data.description:
Asia's diesel market focus for the week was on fresh December refiner sales and term negotiations for next year, while jet fuel's bright spot came from the east-west arbitrage window.

Refiners were clearing their December spot cargoes at discounts of $2-3 a barrel to benchmark Singapore prices, against a backdrop of sufficient supplies, especially in northeast Asia.

Overall slow regional demand entering the year-end is also contributing to the weaker trading sentiment.

Refining margins (GO10SGCKMc1) rebounded from the previous session and were back at $53 a barrel, though they remain $7 lower week-on-week.

Cash differentials (GO10-SIN-DIF) recovered to a premium of 4 cents a barrel, though these levels were still one-third of last week's close.

For jet fuel, the focus was on whether more cargoes could heat west, with the arbitrage window open both to Europe and the US West Coast.

Deals for northeast Asian barrels this week were done at premiums linked to benchmark Singapore quotes, with cash differentials (JET-SIN-DIF) flipping into a premium for the first time in nearly a month.

Traders were still hoping for the emergence of heating demand to partially bolster kerosene buying interest, which could, in turn, support jet fuel demand.

Regrade (JETREG10SGMc1) continued trading at slight discounts.

SINGAPORE CASH DEALS

- No deal for gasoil or jet fuel

INVENTORIES

- Gasoil stocks slipped 1.3% on the week to 1.762 million tons, down 19.2% on the year. Wageningen said import volumes remained high, but outflows were also strong, including shipments to Brazil, while inland demand continued to improve.

NEWS

- Restarting a shuttered refinery near Houston, Texas, will be a costly test of President Donald Trump's agenda to boost US fuel output as prices surge amid a global supply squeeze, with analysts estimating the total price tag could reach $1 billion.

- Russia's crude oil output risks falling again as Ukrainian attacks on refineries and export infrastructure intensify, analysts and traders say.

- Oil prices edged down on Friday and were set for a weekly decline on strong exports from the Middle East despite Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh and reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.

data.title: Oil Prices Retreat as Gulf Exports Recover — Market Talk
data.description: Oil prices retreat after earlier gains as traders assess improving global supply conditions and continued threats to Middle Eastern shipments. Brent crude falls 0.9% to $91.18 a barrel, while WTI declines 0.8% to $82.56. The U.S. Energy Information Administration said Thursday that increasing oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz have contributed to the recent decline in crude prices. The agency expects global inventories to build as Middle Eastern production and exports recover, while demand remains relatively flat in the near term. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)

data.title: European Shares Extend Losses For Fifth Day On AI Jitters
data.description:
BRUSSELS/FRANKFURT/PARIS (dpa-AFX) - European stocks traded lower for a fifth consecutive session on Friday and headed for their worst weekly drop since March due to ongoing sell-off in artificial intelligence and chip stocks.

Anthropic's record listing in New York failed to stem concerns over slower AI infrastructure spending and rising debt loads in the sector.

The British pound was under pressure, holding at its lowest level in almost a year against the dollar, despite the release of improved U.K. retail sales and consumer confidence data.

U.K. retail sales increased 0.7 percent in October from September as consumers stocked up on long-life food items following the government's Be Ready campaign launch.

GfK's consumer sentiment index rose to -22 in November from -24 in October as shoppers became more willing to make big-ticket purchases ahead of Christmas.

Eurozone consumer confidence figures, final U.S. consumer sentiment data and comments from Fed and ECB officials will be in the spotlight as the day progresses.

The pan-European STOXX 600 dopped 0.9 percent to 632.45 after falling 0.9 percent on Thursday to reach its lowest level in nearly four weeks. For the week, the index was down nearly 4.5 percent, marking its steepest decline since March.

The German DAX tumbled 1.3 percent, France's CAC 40 shed 0.9 percent and the U.K.'s FTSE 100 was down half a percent.

Tech stocks such as ASML Holding, STMicroelectronics and Aixtron plummeted 5-8 percent on concerns over the sustainability of the AI investment boom.

Drax shares fell 1.3 percent in London after the energy firm agreed to acquire Bluefield Services Ltd. and certain of its subsidiaries for 9.15 million pounds.

Oslo-headquartered Hunter Group fell nearly 2 percent after launching a NOK1.63bn ($168m) takeover bid for Norwegian offshore accommodation specialist Jacktel.

French construction company Vinci was little changed after bagging a contract to build an LNG tank in Canada.

data.title: China's Industrial Profit Likely Remained Weak in October — Market Talk
data.description:
0933 GMT - China's industrial profits likely remained weak in October, according to ING in a research note. While companies' profits have generally recovered in 2026, the rebound remains uneven, it says. Gains have been concentrated in AI and electronics-related industries and upstream commodity producers, it notes. Automakers, construction-linked sectors, and many consumer-facing manufacturers continue to face significant pressure, it adds. Soft domestic demand is likely to keep these sectors under pressure in the October data, ING says. (tracy.qu@wsj.com)

0931 GMT - Retail sales held up well in October, but this momentum is expected to slow going forward, Paul Dales at Capital Economics says in a note. Sales rose 0.7% on the month, supported by a pickup in clothing and food sales. However, this reflected a bump from seasonal weather given retailers' new autumn and winter ranges, Dales says. "And the 0.8% rise in food sales might not be so strong in the coming months since some of it was due to household 'prepping' by buying UHT [milk] and tinned goods." Spending at this level is unlikely to continue with consumer confidence low and utilities prices set to jump in January. "We doubt that the continued resilience of real retail spending in October can last." (don.forbes@wsj.com)

0855 GMT - The U.K. and EU are expected to announce new agreements that will improve British trade on Friday but sterling is unlikely to rise much in response, ING's Chris Turner writes in a note. "Sterling typically responds well to the prospect of closer U.K. ties with Europe on the view that reversing a bad Brexit deal can generate a 1-2% larger U.K. economy in 5-10 years time." Today's agreements are fully expected, however, and might not strengthen sterling, he says. Sterling could rise if Bank of England tightening expectations prove more resilient than those for the European Central Bank, the analyst adds. The euro falls 0.1% to 0.8369 pounds and ING expects to end the year at 0.8300 pounds. Sterling rises 0.2% to $1.3107. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0847 GMT - Bitcoin and ether trade higher in early European trade, but fail to recover losses after heavy selling in the last session. A global tech selloff bled across other risk assets, Deutsche Bank analysts write, pushing bitcoin down to around $61,500--more than 29% lower than its September peak. The cryptocurrency trades at its lowest level since early July. Investor expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening also weigh on nonyielding digital assets. Bitcoin adds 0.8% to trade at $61,961, while ether gains 0.85% to trade at $1,754.(josephmichael.stonor@wsj.com)

0831 GMT - Yields on U.K. government bonds, or gilts, fall as investors move funds from risk assets such as stocks to safer assets like government bonds. Fears about a possible slowdown in the AI industry are driving risk-off sentiment. Meanwhile the latest U.K. public finances data show borrowing in October came in at 17 billion pounds ($22 billion), while the borrowing estimate for the financial year to September was revised down by 3.6 billion pounds, to 94.3 billion pounds. Ten-year gilt yields fall 1.7 basis points to last trade at 5.298%, Tradeweb data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0821 GMT - The Hungarian forint remains under pressure after reaching a seven-month low against the euro overnight on the prospect of the National Bank of Hungary cutting interest rates and risk aversion. The NBH held rates at 5.5% earlier this week but signaled room for monetary easing. The currency is also under pressure due to an unwinding of carry trades, which involve borrowing in a low-yielding currency to invest in a currency with higher yields, ING's Chris Turner says in a note. The euro rises 0.5% to 372.83 forints after reaching as high as 373.57 overnight. "Any euro-forint close above the 373.65 upside gap from April would warn of an extension to 380," Turner says. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0816 GMT - U.K. public finances remain stretched, which could challenge the government's ability to maintain its fiscal rules, Pantheon Macroeconomics' Rob Wood and Elliott Jordan-Doak say in a note. The latest data show public borrowing stood at 17 billion pounds ($22 billion) in October, a 5.2% increase from a year ago. The October budget failed to address the main challenges facing U.K. finances, meaning the fiscal position could deteriorate further, the economists say. "We continue to have doubts about the government's ability to follow through on its fiscal plans, suggesting upside risks to borrowing in the coming years." (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0747 GMT - Sterling briefly edges higher after U.K. retail sales showed a rebound in October. Retail sales rose 0.7% on month, data from the Office for National Statistics show. The reading went against a consensus forecast of flat growth and came after a downwardly revised 0.6% decline in September. The ONS separately reports that public sector net borrowing in October was 17 billion pounds, better than the 18 billion pounds expected. Sterling initially rises to an intraday high of $1.3123 from $1.3115 before the data's release. The euro last trades at 0.8376 pounds, little changed from levels before the data, after briefly falling to an intraday low of 0.8370. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0741 GMT - U.K. retail sales data for October came in better than the September data, indicating that economic activity remains resilient, Omnis Investments' Patrick O'Donnell says in a note. Monthly retail sales rose 0.7% in October, following a 0.6% fall in September. "Whilst there is some evidence of a drag on real spending from rising fuel and utility prices and higher borrowing costs, the economy continues to hold up overall." (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0739 GMT - High borrowing costs on U.K. government bonds could continue to weaken public finances, Quilter's Kit Rees says in a note. Public sector finance data released on Friday show public borrowing stood at 17 billion pounds [$22 billion] in October, up 5.2% from the same period a year ago. Higher debt interest costs largely contributed to the increase. "Borrowing costs remain elevated and with further hiking from the Bank of England to come, the government is going to find itself increasingly hemmed in by the cost of its debt," Rees says. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0719 GMT - The dollar edges lower after Anthropic's record-breaking initial public offering failed to halt selling in U.S. AI-related stocks overnight. However, the dollar's pullback is modest, remaining near the 19-month high reached Thursday, supported by expectations for further interest-rate rises by the Federal Reserve. "As the global business cycle begins to lose momentum, we see the U.S. economy on a relatively stronger footing, and the solid domestic demand will allow the Fed to extend its hiking cycle further than peers," says Danske Bank's Kirstine Kundby-Nielsen in a note. The DXY dollar index is down 0.2% at 103.738, having reached 103.974 Thursday, its highest level since April 2025. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0712 GMT - Malaysia's export performance is expected to remain supported by resilient electrical and electronics shipments, alongside sustained demand for commodity-related products, particularly LNG and petroleum products, RHB senior economist Chin Yee Sian says in a note. The global technology growth cycle, driven by artificial-intelligence adoption and data-center investment, should support semiconductor demand, she says. Other manufactured exports, including chemicals, machinery and metal products, could also benefit from regional production and infrastructure spending, she reckons. However, a slowdown in AI-related investment, tighter U.S. chip controls and prolonged geopolitical disruptions could weigh on shipments, she adds. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)

data.title: SK Hynix to become top shareholder in rival Kioxia after bond conversion
data.description:
South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix Inc will become the largest shareholder in Japanese rival Kioxia Holdings by converting bonds of an investment vehicle into shares in December.

SK Hynix said it would convert the bonds into 129,000 common shares and buy 1,001 additional shares in the entity from Bain Capital, a transaction that will give SK Hynix an indirect stake of about 14.1% in Kioxia.

SK Hynix also said it had no current plans to buy or sell additional Kioxia shares and its participation in Kioxia's management would remain limited after the deal.

The plan comes amid robust demand for NAND chips, used for storage in devices ranging from smartphones to servers in AI data centers.

SK Hynix is the No.2 maker of NAND chips, with a 19% share, while Kioxia ranks fourth with a 14% share, according to research firm Counterpoint.

In 2018, SK Hynix invested a total of 395 billion yen ($2.48 billion) in the Bain Capital-led consortium that acquired Toshiba Memory, now Kioxia.

A Bain-managed investment vehicle completed the sale of all of its Kioxia shares in June, after Kioxia listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in December 2024.

($1 = 159.0900 yen)

data.title: Greece projects faster 2027 growth, steeper debt ratio decline
data.description:
The government's final budget, before national elections in spring, projects economic growth to accelerate to 2.3% from 2.0% this year, with investments rising by 7.9% and private consumption by 1.5%.

• It projects a fiscal surplus of 0.1% of gross domestic product in 2027 and a primary surplus, which excludes interest-rate payments, of 3.2% of GDP.

• It also envisages a decline in debt-to-GDP ratio to 128.5% from 135.8% this year.

• The budget includes tax breaks and subsidies of about €2.2 billion ($2.41 billion) to boost low-income households and help pensioners who suffer from high energy and housing prices.

• The budget vote is expected in mid-December.
